description: Terminal based IDE & text editor: easy, powerful and fast

summary.one_liner: Fresh is a terminal-based text editor and IDE written in Rust, aimed at VS Code/Sublime-style editing with zero configuration.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a terminal editor with standard keybindings, mouse support, menus, a command palette and fuzzy finder, and no modal editing. It lists multi-cursor editing, block selection, smart indent, undo/redo, and search and replace including query replace and git grep. Navigation covers go-to-line/bracket, position history, bookmarks, and error navigation. It also lists split panes, a file explorer, an integrated terminal, markdown preview, and a Language Server (LSP) client for definitions, references, hover, rename, diagnostics, and autocompletion. An "Orchestrator" feature manages one workspace per git worktree, with terminals and coding agents (claude, codex, opencode, aider). Extensibility is via TypeScript plugins in a sandboxed QuickJS runtime, and the UI is available in multiple languages.
use_cases: editing code in a terminal without learning modal keybindings
opening and navigating very large files
running multiple git worktrees as separate workspaces
searching and replacing across a project with git grep
editing code over SSH or in a remote terminal session
using a language server for code navigation in the terminal
notable: Zero-configuration terminal editor with VS Code/Sublime-style keybindings and no modes
Orchestrator runs one workspace per git worktree, with terminals and coding agents per workspace
Handles multi-gigabyte files with low memory overhead, per the README
Self-updating universal Linux build (fresh --update) with checksum and attestation verification
Sandboxed TypeScript plugin system on QuickJS
caveats: Fresh Desktop builds are unsigned, so macOS and Windows show security prompts on first launch
Telemetry and daily upgrade checks are on by default; must disable with --no-upgrade-check or config
Many install routes; package-manager installs require root and defer updates to that manager
